title: Test instruments and soldering
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: Each basic meter is named after what it measures. A voltmeter measures volts: the electrical push, also called electric potential.
lines.label: volts: the push

lines.caption: A voltmeter connects in parallel, with one lead on each end of the part.
lines.label: voltmeter: in parallel

lines.caption: An ammeter measures current. It connects in series, so the current flows right through it.
lines.label: ammeter: in series

lines.caption: An ohmmeter measures resistance with its own small current, so the circuit must be switched off.
lines.label: power off

lines.caption: A multimeter does all three jobs in one box: voltage, current and resistance.
lines.label: three meters in one

lines.caption: When you solder, use rosin-core solder, never acid-core. A good joint is bright and shiny, not rough and lumpy.
lines.label: rosin core only
